cause: Submission fingerprint concatenated variable-length plan collections without framing, so distinct plans could share one idempotency identity.
invariant: Every scalar and collection element contributes framed length and value bytes to the submission fingerprint.

cause: Successor events could be inserted before the successor execution row required by their execution foreign key.
invariant: A transaction persists every successor execution before any event or action that references its execution_ref, and a missing successor rolls the whole transition back.

cause: Mutation validation accepted the original claim token after its lease expired when no new worker had yet completed takeover.
invariant: An expired claim cannot mutate state; only a newly acquired claim with matching token, worker, attempt and live lease may write.

cause: The temporal boundary between dispatch/capacity waiting and provider execution was ambiguous, so queue time could be confused with provider runtime.
invariant: Dispatching capacity wait consumes no provider timeout; StartedAt and DeadlineAt are fixed at launch acceptance, remain stable during observe, and only then bound pending attempts and timeout.

cause: A public execution and launch-request contract changed while the focal gate omitted downstream bootstrap consumers, leaving an obsolete singular field and a slice compared with struct equality.
invariant: Every public contract change compiles all internal consumers, and test fakes compare slice-bearing requests with semantic equality before the change can integrate.

cause: A completion could carry an operation timestamp from inside the claim lease even though artifact persistence finished after that lease expired, allowing a backdated state commit attempt.
invariant: Claim validity is checked at the actual transactional commit boundary; artifact persistence crossing LeaseUntil cannot commit success, attestations, artifacts or action completion with an earlier timestamp.

cause: A subagent used the repository-wide `go test ./...` wildcard, crossed the isolated rebuild boundary and started historical test binaries before the process group was terminated.
invariant: Every canonical rebuild verification command enumerates only safe product packages; a bare `./...` wildcard is forbidden because the frozen legacy tree contains opt-in real smokes.

cause: Two semantic-review shards retained 450 capability mappings through generated fallback branches and templated reasons while reporting every row as independently reviewed.
invariant: An independent semantic receipt is counted only after subject-specific judgment; generated keep-current fallbacks and the five known canned confirmations are rejected, and an adversarial pass rechecks the whole affected universe.

cause: Historical bug emission flags returned from the test before comparing the extracted occurrences or IDs with their canonical ledgers, allowing an inherited environment variable to create a false green.
invariant: Traceability emission flags are output-only diagnostics and can never return, skip or replace canonical ledger validation.

cause: The historical bug policy named a nonexistent `accepted_capabilities` JSON fragment while the gate silently read `capability_entries` through separate code.
invariant: Every declared capability authority resolves to the exact non-empty JSON collection consumed by its gate; policy and implementation cannot use different names.

cause: Task and bug source universes were expanded from their own pending-source manifest, so legacy Markdown outside those patterns could disappear without making the gate fail.
invariant: A filesystem-derived census must partition every legacy Markdown source into explicit cumulative roles and fail on any absent, duplicated or digest-drifted source before semantic ledgers can be accredited.

cause: Twenty-eight Markdown files containing literal BUG-ORQ references were outside the bug role, leaving hundreds of exact occurrences invisible to the historical incident ledger.
invariant: Every literal BUG-ORQ occurrence in the fixed legacy Markdown filesystem scope must resolve to an exact occurrence, range alias expansion or reviewed exclusion independent of the source manifest.

cause: The traceability JSON Schema was included in evidence only by file hash and never compiled or applied to every canonical JSON document and JSONL row.
invariant: The canonical schema must compile and validate every governed JSON document and every JSONL row, while adversarial invalid fixtures are demonstrably rejected.

cause: Acceptance receipts verified candidate hashes but omitted trusted execution metadata such as structured argv, exit code, output digest, Go version and source-tree identity.
invariant: A release receipt must bind the immutable candidate to a reproducible command execution with structured argv, zero exit code, output hash, toolchain, source-tree identity and bounded timestamp without including itself.

cause: A candidate-review shard claimed policy validation while emitting a nonexistent exclusion code and assigning broad audit findings outside the independently adjudicated actionable ranges as executable work.
invariant: Every candidate decision is checked against canonical reason codes; every counterreview row carries fixture digest, reviewer, method and transition provenance and binds one-to-one to its exact input and final decision; reviewed narrative blocks retain exact entry coverage without excluding strict historical candidates.

cause: The rebuild write-set guard still allowed only the original monolithic traceability test and omitted the split V03 root tests and acceptance surface, so its final check rejected authorized rebuild files.
invariant: The behavioral write-set gate accepts every current rebuild-owned surface while continuing to reject frozen legacy roots in an isolated Git repository.

cause: Markdown review batches were hashed and counted, but their decisions were not bound as exact per-source receipts in the canonical source-role rows, so aggregate completeness could hide a missing, duplicated or altered review.
invariant: Every manual Markdown classification carries the exact review_ref, classification and reason from one fixture row; every fixture row is consumed once; conflicting classifications require an explicit adjudication.

cause: The roadmap accredited capabilities from evidence that proved only shared infrastructure or a narrower vertical, overstating product readiness.
invariant: Accredited status requires direct evidence for the exact capability; partial or shared evidence leaves the capability declared, routes it to its owning future vertical and carries no premature evidence refs.

cause: Planned acceptance contracts exposed syntactically runnable go test commands, so tooling or operators could execute a placeholder and mistake its result for acceptance of the vertical.
invariant: Every planned acceptance command is explicitly prefixed planned: and is non-runnable; only a contract with executable status may expose a shell-runnable validation command.

cause: The source-integration vertical was treated as causally accredited by a hardcoded ID exception even though AC-V01 had no durable receipt.
invariant: Every executable contract declares a canonical receipt path; a vertical with no owned capabilities becomes a causal prerequisite only through that receipt-backed contract; and the post-execution gate validates the real V2 receipt cryptographically without requiring it before issuance.

cause: The planned V04 acceptance command omitted the acceptance package and named only a generic nonexistent test, so promoting it mechanically could produce a green that never ran its declared acceptance file.
invariant: Every executable acceptance command includes the package that owns its declared test_ref; a contract cannot become executable while its command bypasses that package.

cause: A domain subagent briefly edited internal/goal/intent_test.go outside its declared write-set before the integrator detected the expansion and the agent reverted its own hunk.
invariant: Every path changed after a vertical's red checkpoint is declared in that vertical's candidate_subjects or an exact governed evidence/handoff exclusion before a receipt can be issued.
evidence_ref: failed:V04 implementation delta is intentionally incomplete and candidate_subjects must be reconciled before seal

cause: A provider spec_hash mismatch was treated as ordinary execution failure and closed the Goal, turning crossed or unverifiable evidence into a false terminal result.
invariant: A required, invalid or mismatched provider spec_hash quarantines the causal action, leaves the Goal nonterminal and persists no artifact, attestation or closure.

cause: Submit and Amend accepted a repository response marked created=true when it returned a semantically similar but different Goal snapshot, allowing authoritative refs, hashes or timestamps to be substituted after application construction.
invariant: For created=true the repository result must exactly equal the application-built Goal snapshot and executions and contain no unexpected evidence; created=false replay remains semantically validated.

cause: Launch receipt validation compared spec_hash with the request before classifying an empty or noncanonical value, collapsing required and invalid failures into mismatch and leaving those quarantine branches untested.
invariant: Receipt spec_hash validation is ordered required, canonical, then causal equality; application quarantine tests cover every receipt classification.

cause: The SQLite AppSpec confirmation trigger required confirmed_by to equal the Intent actor even though the domain contract permits a distinct authenticated reviewer, making the persistence adapter narrower than the core and blocking the future reviewer role.
invariant: Concrete persistence may enforce AppSpec time, integrity and scope invariants but must accept every domain-valid confirmed_by principal; authorization remains an application or composition policy.

cause: The V2 to V3 AppSpec backfill validated only Intent integrity and copied Goal lifecycle rows without restoring the complete aggregate, allowing a SQL-valid but domain-invalid Goal to receive migration receipt 3 and fail only on a later read.
invariant: Before migration receipt and user_version advance, every migrated Goal must be readable and domain-valid through the canonical V3 reconstruction path inside the same transaction; any invalid aggregate rolls schema, data, receipt and version back to V2.

cause: The V04 fixture declared the canonical initial AppSpec reason operator.initial_confirmation, while application hardcoded initial_confirmation and acceptance never consumed the fixture field, so a different spec hash could pass green.
invariant: Every semantically active acceptance fixture field is bound to executable behavior; the initial AppSpec reason has one canonical namespaced value shared by acceptance and application.

cause: The executable V04 command filtered for TestV04 names although the Goal, provider-port, fake and SQLite AppSpec behavioral tests used older names; those packages reported no tests to run, while changed Codex and i18n packages were omitted entirely.
invariant: An executable vertical command must run behavioral tests, not compilation alone, in every owned package and changed adapter included in its candidate; a package reporting no matching tests cannot support an acceptance receipt.
evidence_ref: failed:V04 command reported no tests to run for goal ports fake and sqlite and omitted codex and i18n

cause: The V04 candidate coverage gate compared its opening commit with the live working tree forever, so any legitimate V05 path would retroactively fail the sealed V04 contract and prevent independent vertical evolution.
invariant: Before issuance candidate coverage checks the complete live delta; the sealed contract freezes that delta at an existing descendant commit and later vertical paths cannot alter V04, while any change to a V04 candidate still invalidates its content receipt.
evidence_ref: failed:current TestV04CandidateSubjectsCoverCommittedDelta always diffs base_git_head against the live worktree and has no sealed delta boundary

cause: After confirmation and spec_hash became mandatory, bootstrap E2E direct Submit callers still omitted Confirm and test agent doubles returned receipts or observations without echoing the authoritative hash; the old V04 command never executed those compositions.
invariant: Every composition and test double must consume the same confirmed application contract and provider hash boundary as production; the unfiltered bootstrap suite must close real MCP, DAG, restart, shutdown and shared-artifact paths before V04 can issue evidence.
